clue.text: Male celebrity has to stand before monarch as ceremonial officer

indicators.note: before places the word for stand ahead of the monarch in the answer

parts.note: an ace is a star performer, a celebrity in a field
to bear is to stand or tolerate
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A famous man must wait in line before the king or queen at some formal ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A dignitary carrying a ceremonial staff of office in processions is a ceremonial official.

clue.text: Factory with a thousand unable to work?

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
someone ill is off sick and unable to work

explanation.surface: A factory with a thousand staff off sick and unable to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill is a building where goods such as cloth or paper are manufactured, a works.

clue.text: Cold fare I ate — horrible restaurant

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: horrible suggests the letters of fare I ate are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the cold food eaten at a restaurant was horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges FARE I ATE into AFETERIA, which follows C.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service eating place is a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Boat Inn starts to get expensive

parts.note: a bar is a drinking place, like an inn

indicators.note: starts to tells us to take the opening letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: A riverside pub begins to get pricey.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed vessel used on canals and rivers is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Essentially a threat to be averted

indicators.note: averted, turned aside, suggests the letters of a threat are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fundamentally, this is a danger that should be headed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep down or fundamentally is an idiom meaning essentially, in one's true nature.

clue.text: Intellectual, say — good person to lead school?

parts.note: e.g., for example, is signalled by say
the head is the person in charge of a school

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bright, decent person should be made a head teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially a brainy, bookish person is called this, a highbrow.

clue.text: Image I would love — new one in car?

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a novice driver displays an L plate, the learner sign, on the car

explanation.surface: Someone muses about a picture they would like to have in a new car.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a carved or graven image worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Tot and adult creating form of entertainment

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram
A is the film classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A toddler and a grown-up put on a show together.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays performed on stage or screen are a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Nasty team insult just before the final whistle?

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of team insult are made into an ugly rearrangement

explanation.surface: A football side hurls a vicious insult as the match is about to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening at the very end of an allotted time, as in a match about to finish, is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Performance needs superior accomplice, in fact

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage
U stands for upper class, socially superior
an ally is a partner or accomplice

explanation.surface: A show needs a top-notch sidekick, it is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Really, as a matter of truth, is what both expressions mean.

clue.text: Line at start of famous poem about returning prisoner

indicators.note: at start of puts the letter for line ahead of the poem

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem

indicators.note: returning tells us the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A poem's opening line is about a convict coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: If— is Rudyard Kipling's much-loved poem of advice; 'returning' turns the word for about round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone serving a life sentence is a long-term prisoner.

clue.text: Superior school form

definitions.meaning: second sense: a senior year group

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means of the finest quality, and can also be read literally as an upper form in a school.

clue.text: 'Cheap' accommodation almost exorbitant? Then show anger

indicators.note: almost says the word for exorbitant loses its final letter

parts.note: a steep price is an exorbitant one
to rage is to show fury

explanation.surface: Budget lodging is nearly overpriced, and a guest gets furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest-fare passenger quarters on a ship were cheap accommodation for travellers.

clue.text: Remove something potentially harmful from part of lunar module

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking a dangerous item off a section of the moon lander.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm, taking weapons away, is to remove something that could cause harm.

clue.text: Stop in one street and another? I will

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a second street, another St
I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: Someone promises to halt in one road and then another.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt, with no movement, is a stop.

clue.text: Assembled group dismissed after performance

indicators.note: after places the word for dismissed behind the word for performance

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act or spot on a bill
in cricket a batter dismissed is out

explanation.surface: A gathered crowd is sent away once the show ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' looks like a verb acting on the group, but it is the cricket sense of a batter being given out.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of people who come to an event is the assembled group attending.

clue.text: Excessively adventurous series of deliveries completed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries; when it is done, the over has been bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket over finishes, with a nod to a reckless bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six balls bowled by one bowler; 'over bowled' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Too daring, beyond what is sensible, is excessively adventurous.

clue.text: Creature in hold knocked out, keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping says the shuffled letters hold the quiet sign inside
knocked out suggests the letters of in hold are battered into a new shape

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An animal in a ship's hold has been stunned and is not making a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creature in hold' reads as one phrase, but 'in' joins the fodder; the rearranged letters are DOLHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This intelligent marine mammal is an example of a creature.

clue.text: Source of iron? Unfortunately, I hate meat

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of I hate meat come out in an unlucky jumble

explanation.surface: A vegetarian laments being unable to get iron from meat they hate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests diet, but the source of iron is a mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: This red mineral is the chief ore from which iron is extracted.

clue.text: Take food in home that's comfortable and with the least clutter

indicators.note: in places the eating inside the cosy home

parts.note: a nest is a snug, comfortable home
to eat is to take food

explanation.surface: Eating at home in comfort with everything tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: The tidiest, most orderly place has the least clutter.

clue.text: Mad aunt is entertaining this writer in the country

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the shuffled letters hold the writer
mad suggests the letters of aunt is go crazy into a new order

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as this writer, I

explanation.surface: A crazy aunt plays host to the setter while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges AUNT IS to TUNISA; 'entertaining' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital of this North African nation, so it is a country.

clue.text: Settlement apt to be tricky with unknown fellows invading

indicators.note: invading means pushing into, so the other pieces go inside the shuffled letters
tricky suggests the letters of apt are twisted into a new arrangement

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown
men are fellows

explanation.surface: A colonial settlement proves tricky when strangers invade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' suggests a colony, but it means paying a bill; the rearranged letters are PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling a bill is making a payment, so settlement is a synonym.

clue.text: Studied 'Introduction to Plato' with hesitation? Not new!

indicators.note: introduction to means the opening letter of the philosopher's name

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
second-hand goods are used, not new

explanation.surface: A student reads an introductory Plato text haltingly, finding nothing new in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To read something through carefully is to have studied it.

clue.text: Clean up some of the Aussie territory?

definitions.meaning: first sense: to scour or wash hard
second sense: the scrubland or bush covering much of Australia

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to wash vigorously, and also names the low brushwood country of the Australian outback.

clue.text: More than one revolutionary, having got rid of British, dances

indicators.note: having got rid of says the abbreviation for British is dropped from the rebels

parts.note: rebels are revolutionaries

explanation.surface: Insurgents expel the British and celebrate with dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing B from REBELS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively Scottish and Irish folk dances are reels.

clue.text: Bottle with petrol in US may be used as weapon

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage, nerve
Americans call petrol gas

explanation.surface: A bottle of fuel used as a petrol bomb in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, so the surface's petrol bomb is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison gas attacking the nervous system is a chemical weapon.

clue.text: Scottish location excited Nigel

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of Nigel are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Nigel gets worked up about a place in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland, so a Scottish location.

clue.text: Fellow offers some amusing entertainment

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man provides a bit of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman or chap is a colloquial word for a fellow.

clue.text: Impractical types having notion to join combat

parts.note: an idea is a notion
the lists were the arena for jousting, so entering the lists means joining combat

explanation.surface: Dreamers who have an idea about going to war.
explanation.definitionFit: People who pursue perfect principles regardless of reality are impractical types.

clue.text: Mountain leader good on Ben Nevis taking English?

parts.note: guid is the Scots word for good, and Ben Nevis is Scotland's highest mountain

explanation.surface: A climbing guide on Britain's highest peak taking an Englishman up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Nevis stands for Scotland, where 'good' is spelt GUID.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads climbers up a mountain is a mountain guide.

clue.text: Young lady in glasses

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A young woman wearing spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl or young woman is called this, especially in northern England and Scotland.

clue.text: Great Dane's fouled up item of outdoor furniture

indicators.note: fouled up suggests the letters of Great Dane's are messed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A big dog has soiled a bench in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A bench placed on a lawn or patio is outdoor furniture.
